How to make the app the best

  1. Ask family or carer first. Then ask the care type: nanny, babysitter or au pair.
  2. One best pair at a time. The home screen is a full screen card: big photo, score ring, two reasons, a big Book button, one tap Message.
  3. Show the match, not a search box. Both sides score each other. Perfect Pair at 90 and up.
  4. Chat opens on the match. It never waits for a booking.
  5. Trust Passport and Care Passport stay apart. Uploaded is not checked. Verified has a date.
  6. Au pairs: visa on its own. Show ready, in progress or not applied, and where they live now. Families can filter for visa ready or already here.
  7. Photos shown whole. Never children faces.
  8. All settings in Settings. No donations anywhere.
  9. Check every real screen against this mock with screenshots before the next build.

Patterns that win

  • A big face first. Trust starts with photos.
  • Checks shown as badges, with dates.
  • One main button. Book.
  • Message always in reach.
  • Map for nearby, list for choice, deck for speed.

The matching engine

Two sides score each other. The score is the middle. Money never adds points.

6 steps

  1. Must haves first. Blue Card or police check, first aid, licence, pets. Miss one and the person goes to a "Nearly" list.
  2. Pay check. The offer must reach the carer's lowest rate. It is a check, not points.
  3. Six scores from 0 to 1: days and hours, style, skills, language, place, activities.
  4. Weights. The family can change them. They always add to 100.
  5. Both sides. Family score and carer score. We take the average.
  6. Label. 90 and up Perfect Pair. 80 to 89 Strong Fit. 65 to 79 Good Fit.

Au pairs

Days and hours become start date, stay and weekly hours. The working holiday limit (6 months with one family) shows as a small gap, not a block. Home offers (own room, car, bonus) match what the au pair wants.

Visa

Shown on its own: ready, in progress, not applied. A family can switch on Visa ready only or Already in Australia. It never changes the percent.

What a carer needs, and how an au pair gets a visa. The app shows the right check for each place.

Rows marked Confirm come from memory or a thin source. Check the official page before the app states them as fact.

How the app uses this

  • The family's place picks the check name: Blue Card in Queensland, a police check from the home country for au pairs.
  • Every au pair profile shows a visa line: Visa ready (grant letter sighted, with date), In progress, Not applied, or Citizen or resident.
  • It also shows where they live now and when they can arrive.
  • A family can filter for Visa ready only and Already in the country.
  • Visa never changes the match percent.

What I changed and why

Short and simple.

Changed

  • Family or carer is asked first.
  • One best pair on a full screen, with the score.
  • Big Book button. One tap Message.
  • Photos are shown whole.
  • Why you match is on every card.
  • Visa and checks shown plainly for au pairs.
  • A luxury map: soft pink, cream and sky, with the bunny pins.
  • Donations are gone. No menu item, no page, no rainbow, no wall.

Why

  • Families want the right person fast, and to trust them.
  • Carers want fair pay and a good fit, and to say yes fast.
  • Au pairs want to know the visa is real.
  • Fewer taps means more bookings.

How payments work (recommended)

Use Stripe Connect with Express accounts. Each carer sets up a Stripe account in a few taps, and Stripe does the identity check. The family pays when they book. We hold the money, then send it to the carer once the shift or trial day is done. This is Stripe's "separate charges and transfers" way, and Stripe says Express accounts support it.

The percentage: keep 10 percent, paid by the family on top, carer gets 100 percent. It matches the 13 Nov ruling, it is simple to explain, and carers see their full rate. Care.com charges 12 percent (found in research), so 10 is fair. Do not take a cut from carers.

Example: 4 hour trial at $42
Carer gets$168.00
Family pays (168 plus 10 percent)$184.80
Stripe card fee, from Stripe's list price of 2.9 percent plus 30 centsabout $5.66
Stripe payout fee, 0.25 percent plus 25 centsabout $0.67
Left for Caresitters, before the $2 a month per active carerabout $10.47

Fees are from stripe.com/connect/pricing and Stripe's account types page. Check your own Stripe dashboard for the real Australian rate.

Still to check: how long Stripe lets you hold money before sending it on, and whether Australian rules need a licence for holding funds. I did not verify either. Also, I believe Apple does not require its own in app purchase for real world services paid outside the app. Confirm this in Apple's App Review Guidelines before you build.
